clue.text: Beat and sack the clever Jester ?

definitions.meaning: to beat someone by cleverness is to get the better of them
read as two words, an order to throw out the man of wit: put the wit out

explanation.surface: A clever court fool is thrashed and dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent by cunning is to outsmart them; split in two, the word tells you to turf out the wit.

clue.text: Symbol of a famous hiding

parts.note: the gall worn on Royal Oak Day recalls Charles II hiding in a tree after Worcester

explanation.definitionFit: Royalists wore an oak gall on 29 May to commemorate Charles II hiding in the Boscobel oak.

clue.text: He demonstrates an early form 'of motion

definitions.text: He demonstrates an early form 'of motion

parts.words: He demonstrates an early form 'of motion
parts.note: a small child shows the first, unsteady way of walking

explanation.definitionFit: A child just learning to walk moves in an early, wobbly way.

clue.text: One girl, one friend ?—-Far from lively !

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
Nan is a girl's name
one is I, the Roman numeral
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A girl, her friend and the speaker are anything but lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, the opposite of lively.

clue.text: M. Poirot has a point — a strong one

parts.note: Agatha Christie's detective is Hercule Poirot
S, south, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Agatha Christie's detective makes a forceful argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a strong one' defines the mythical strongman, while 'has' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero famed for his twelve labours is the byword for physical might.

clue.text: Remotely descriptive of the Polar Regions

definitions.text: Remotely descriptive of the Polar Regions

parts.words: Remotely descriptive of the Polar Regions
parts.note: the poles are literally the two extremities of the globe, and the phrase means the remotest places

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the farthest-flung places, and the poles are where the globe ends.

clue.text: Lengthy communication

parts.note: a telegram, sent down a long wire, which is also a nautical measure of length

explanation.definitionFit: A cablegram is a message, and a cable is also a measured length at sea.

clue.text: One turns in, embraced by volcanic issue of Mrs Aeneas

indicators.note: embraced by puts the first pieces inside the volcanic outflow

parts.note: lava is what issues from a volcano
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: turns says the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns in, surrounded by molten rock from a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Aeneas' is the wife of Virgil's hero: in the Aeneid he weds Lavinia, daughter of King Latinus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's epic the Trojan hero marries the Latin princess Lavinia.

clue.text: A scene-shifter philosopher

indicators.note: a scene-shifter moves the stage scenery, so the words a scene have their letters moved about

explanation.surface: A stagehand who moves sets is also a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman Stoic philosopher.

clue.text: They are' made for roulette tables and home industry

definitions.text: They are' made for roulette tables
definitions.meaning: the revolving wheels on which the roulette ball runs
the cottage device for making yarn

explanation.surface: Items crafted both for the casino and for cottage craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is played on revolving wheels, and yarn was once made at home on a wheel worked by foot.

clue.text: Reading which made the laddie doze off

parts.note: a laddie is a boy, a kid
to doze off is to have napped

explanation.surface: A book that sent a young Scots lad to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Reading' is Robert Louis Stevenson's novel of the Scottish lad David Balfour; 'which made' only links the book to the pun on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's adventure novel is a famous piece of reading matter.

clue.text: One could say that his boys were minors

definitions.text: One could say that his boys were minors

parts.words: One could say that his boys were minors
parts.note: the wartime minister whose conscripted young men were sent down the coal mines, so his boys were miners

explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Bevin, wartime Minister of Labour, sent young conscripts to work in coal mines; they were called his Boys.

clue.text: For some, the driving seat?

parts.note: the seat behind the rider of a motorcycle, from which some passengers try to direct the driving

explanation.definitionFit: The passenger seat behind a motorcyclist is where a back-seat driver of a bike sits.

clue.text: Chief has a nice arrangement with deep implication

parts.note: OC, officer commanding, is the chief of a unit

indicators.note: an arrangement of the words a nice puts their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: The boss has made a pleasant arrangement with a hidden meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief' is OC, the army's officer commanding; 'with deep implication' means relating to the deep, the sea, not profound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to do with the ocean relates to the deep, the sea.

clue.text: Do with one heroine here?

parts.note: put the word Do with one to get the surname of Blackmore's heroine, and this light supplies her first name

explanation.definitionFit: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so this first name joins Do plus one.

clue.text: Games which show this main difference

indicators.note: making a difference to the words this main alters the order of their letters

explanation.surface: Sports events that reveal this chief distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isthmian Games were ancient Greek contests held at Corinth, on its isthmus.
explanation.definitionFit: These ancient Greek athletic festivals at Corinth bear the adjective as their name.

clue.text: Emma and a Lord are involved on the stage

indicators.note: words that are involved are tangled together, mixing their letters

explanation.surface: Emma and an aristocrat are romantically entangled in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational play with stock villains and heroes is a stage genre.

clue.text: Wight ?

parts.note: wight is an old word for a person, here one from the Isle of Wight

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A wight is an old word for a person; a person of the Isle of Wight lives on an isle.

clue.text: Induce to give in perhaps to the French

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: perhaps says the word give may be shown in some other order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Persuade someone to surrender, perhaps to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns GIVE into VEIG; the clue's IN comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle someone is to coax or lure them into acting, to persuade by flattery.

clue.text: God next after Uranus ?

definitions.meaning: the Roman god of the sea
the planet beyond Uranus, counting outwards from the Sun

explanation.surface: Who is the deity that follows the sky god?
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman sea deity names the eighth planet, which orbits beyond Uranus.

clue.text: Its fruits are not for the' working classes

definitions.text: Its fruits are not for the' working classes

parts.words: Its fruits are not for the' working classes
parts.note: in Homer, eating this plant's fruit makes men forget work and lie idle

explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters, fed on its fruit, lost all desire to work or go home.

clue.text: Useful in some card hands, they'd cause raised eyebrows at poker

definitions.meaning: in bridge and whist, holdings of the best and third-best cards of a suit

definitions.text: they'd cause raised eyebrows at poker
definitions.meaning: split up, ..., impossible in one honest pack

explanation.surface: Combinations valued at bridge would cause suspicion in a poker game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenace is a bridge holding such as ace-queen; read as ten aces it is too many for one pack.

clue.text: East of Suez Kipling's man can raise one

definitions.text: East of Suez Kipling's man can raise one

parts.words: East of Suez Kipling's man can raise one
parts.note: Kipling's Mandalay soldier longs to be east of Suez where a man can raise a craving for drink

explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's line runs 'Where there aren't no Ten Commandments an' a man can raise a' craving for drink.

clue.text: Hot spot for a sit-in on Friday night?

definitions.text: Hot spot for a sit-in on Friday night?

parts.words: Hot spot for a sit-in on Friday night?
parts.note: a small tub of hot water you sit in, the traditional weekly scrub on a Friday night

explanation.definitionFit: A small portable tub, filled with hot water, in which one sits rather than lies.

clue.text: Ophidian computer ?

definitions.meaning: ophidian means snake-like, here a snake
one who adds up figures, a calculator

explanation.definitionFit: The adder is a venomous snake; someone who totals figures is one who adds.

clue.text: Appendices show, a study, in Dada development

indicators.note: in places the study inside the other letters
a development of the word Dada rearranges its letters

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Extra pages describe a piece of research into the Dada art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' and 'a' are only links; the Dada of the surface is the early twentieth-century art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book, supplements or appendices.

clue.text: Plump Puritan loses his head

indicators.note: loses says a part is taken away from the Puritan's name

parts.note: Roundheads were the Puritan Parliamentarians of the English Civil War
the word head is what he loses

explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Puritan side in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair; 'his head' is the word HEAD, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and rotund both describe a figure that is well filled out.

clue.text: Delighted at being " gated "?

parts.note: gated read as given a gate, a door, so supplied with a way in

explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means enraptured or spellbound; read differently, it is furnished with a doorway.

clue.text: The Circle is in the right — he's a man of ideas

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: in puts the word is inside the abbreviation for right

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political group thinks it is correct, led by a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist deals in ideas and speculation rather than practice.

clue.text: Firearm for a Jerry Tom ?

definitions.meaning: a German make of rifle and pistol
a tomcat that catches mice, given a German spelling, Jerry being slang for German

explanation.surface: A gun suited to a German named Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mauser is a German rifle; a German tom that hunts rodents would be a mouser in Teutonic spelling.
